title: Greeting & small talk
blurb: ¿Cómo andás? is the whole opening move. Learn these and you stop being a stranger.

title: Asking & understanding
blurb: How to not understand, gracefully, and get it repeated slower.

title: Yes, no, maybe
blurb: Wanting, being able, having to, needing. Four verbs that carry whole conversations.

title: Being & feeling
blurb: ser, estar, tener, andar. What you are against how you are.

title: Doing & handling things
blurb: hacer, dar, poner, llevar. The verbs that fit everywhere, which is exactly why they come first.

title: Seeing, hearing & noticing
blurb: ver and mirar are not the same verb, and neither are oír and escuchar.

title: Buying & paying
blurb: Prices run in tens of thousands. These are the verbs attached to the money.

title: Haggling & quantities
blurb: At the market the price is an opening offer, not a fact.

title: Bank, cash & phone credit
blurb: Cargar saldo, sacar plata, transferir. The weekly admin of having money here.

title: Ordering & eating
blurb: From the empanada stand to the asado. The most-repeated verbs of your week.

title: Cooking & the kitchen
blurb: What you do to food before eating it, and what the heat does to it here.

title: Tereré & drinking together
blurb: Cebar, convidar, compartir. The ritual with the highest social return in the country.

title: Transport & the colectivo
blurb: Subir, bajar, parar. Telling a driver where you want to get off.

title: Directions & places
blurb: Distance is counted in cuadras and nobody uses street numbers.

title: Driving & the moto
blurb: Half of Asunción is on two wheels. These are the verbs that go with them.

title: The house & renting
blurb: Alquilar, mudarse, arreglar. Getting a roof and keeping it working.

title: Daily routine
blurb: The reflexive verbs: levantarse, bañarse, acostarse. Your whole day in twenty words.

title: Fixing, breaking & power cuts
blurb: Se cortó la luz is a sentence you will say often. Here is the rest of it.

title: Weather & the heat
blurb: The heat dominates life here, so it dominates the small talk.

title: Family & friends
blurb: Family language carries more social weight here than you are used to.

title: Conversation & opinion
blurb: Saying what you think, agreeing, disagreeing, and telling a story.

title: Feelings & conflict
blurb: Apologising, forgiving, getting annoyed. The repair verbs.

title: Arranging to meet
blurb: Quedar, avisar, cancelar. Plans here are softer than you expect.

title: Free time & interests
blurb: What you do when you are not working. The fastest route out of the expat bubble.

title: Work & tasks
blurb: Getting work done, with other people, and being paid for it.

title: Paperwork & bureaucracy
blurb: Residency, stamps, certificates. You will meet these verbs at a counter.

title: Phone & computer
blurb: Mandar, descargar, conectarse. The verbs of being reachable.

title: Body, illness & the pharmacy
blurb: Symptoms, and asking for something at the farmacia. Dengue is seasonal and real.

title: Emergencies
blurb: The ones you hope stay unused. Worth knowing cold rather than well.

title: Thinking & knowing
blurb: Supposing, doubting, concluding. The verbs of an opinion rather than an action.

title: Change & cause
blurb: Becoming, causing, producing, affecting. The machinery of explanation.

title: Formal & written Spanish
blurb: What you will read rather than say. Contracts, notices, officialdom.

title: News & institutions
blurb: Politics, courts, money at scale. For the radio and the newspaper.
